title: The Quiet Typewriter
premise: In the winter of 1911, widowed lighthouse keeper Lena Underhill lives a deliberately small life on the fog-bound coast, keeping her late husband's typewriter as her only companion. When a half-frozen stranger, Elias Voss, washes ashore carrying letters typed on that very machine—letters proving her husband faked his death to expose a shipping conspiracy—Lena must decide whether the man she mourned ever existed. Together they smuggle the evidence inland past three checkpoints before the river ice breaks and the conspirators' men can cross freely. At the final checkpoint, Lena learns her husband is alive and chose silence over returning; she delivers the truth anyway, choosing justice over the ghost of belonging.
about_author: Bram Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse service records along the northern coast. He writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of events they never asked for.

chapters.title: The Man in the Wrack Line
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. During the worst storm of the season, Lena finds Elias half-drowned among the wrack below her lighthouse and nurses him against her better judgment. Among his effects she discovers letters typed unmistakably on her dead husband's machine, signed with his private nickname for her. The emotional beat is disorientation: grief cracking open into suspicion that everything she mourned was staged.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Lena and Elias. Elias reveals he was her husband's courier in an investigation of drowned sailors and falsified manifests, and that men are already searching the coast for him. Lena tests his story against her own memories of her marriage. The beat is reluctant alliance: two strangers bound by a dead man's secrets, deciding to move before the thaw traps them.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, then shared. They travel inland by sledge and night roads, bribing, bluffing, and slipping past the first two checkpoints, but at the third Lena recognizes the inspector as a friend of her husband's—and realizes the searchers know exactly whose widow she is. The climax arrives when she confronts the truth: her husband lives, hiding, and let her grieve. The beat is betrayal sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Breakup
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With the ice groaning apart, Lena chooses to deliver the evidence herself rather than flee with Elias or wait for her husband's permission to matter. She hands the letters to a magistrate as the river opens, then returns to her light—not invisible anymore, but keeper of something larger than her own grief. The resolution beat is quiet, hard-won self-belonging.
